constraints: Don't modify nums; O(1) extra space.

examples.explain: The duplicate may appear many times.

hints: A set or sorting solves it, but both break the rules (extra space, or modifying the array).
Treat each index as a node with an edge i → nums[i]. Why must this graph contain a cycle?
Floyd's algorithm: find a meeting point with slow/fast pointers, then restart one from 0 - they meet at the cycle entrance.

insight.mnemonic: Two arrows into one node make a loop - find where the loop starts.
insight.oneLiner: Follow i → nums[i] from index 0; the duplicate is the entrance of the cycle, found with Floyd's two phases.
insight.pattern: Array as a linked list + Floyd's cycle entrance

recall.a: 1: slow/fast until they meet. 2: reset one pointer to the start; step both by 1 until they meet - that's the entrance.
No value is 0, so nothing points into index 0 - it's outside the cycle, like a list head.

insight.why: n + 1 indices map into n values, so two indices share a target (pigeonhole). That shared target is where the cycle begins.

oneLiner: Follow i → nums[i] from index 0; the duplicate is the entrance of the cycle, found with Floyd's two phases.

pitfalls.explain: Sorting or marking nums in place is not allowed - the follow-up is about O(1) space without mutation.
pitfalls.title: Modified the input

pitfalls.explain: Where slow and fast meet is somewhere in the cycle. Restart one pointer from 0 and walk both by one step.
pitfalls.title: Returned the meeting point instead of the entrance

solutions.idea: Return the first value seen twice. Simple, but uses O(n) memory.
solutions.name: Hash set

footnotes.text: Floyd's theorem: the distance from the start to the cycle's entrance equals the distance from the meeting point to the entrance (going around the loop). Stepping both pointers one at a time, they meet exactly at the entrance - which is the duplicated value.

solutions.idea: Treat the array as a linked list i → nums[i]; the duplicate is where its cycle begins.
solutions.name: Floyd's cycle detection

class Solution:
    def findDuplicate(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
statement:
`nums` has `n + 1` integers, each in the range `[1, n]`. Exactly **one value is repeated** (possibly more than twice). Return that value.

Do it **without modifying `nums`** and using only **O(1) extra space**.
title: Find the Duplicate Number
